family.name: Copywriter / Content Writer
family.summary: A launch brief with real customer research: find the insight competitors miss, handle a client who wants an unprovable “No. 1” claim, and edit a weak landing page.

stages.title: Warm-up
stages.summary: A 45-second spontaneous answer. Not scored; gives a voice sample to compare with later recordings.

stages.title: Three headline directions
stages.summary: Write three headline directions from the research and pick one. Tests finding the insight competitors miss. Think aloud.

stages.title: The client's "No. 1" line
stages.summary: The client insists on an unprovable superlative. Tests judgement with a client. Think aloud.

stages.title: After it goes live
stages.summary: Consequences of their choice. Tests adapting and ownership.

stages.title: Edit a weak landing page
stages.summary: A draft with jargon, a buried benefit, an unsupported claim and inconsistent voice. Think aloud.

stages.title: Search ads (AI allowed)
stages.summary: Write search ad variations with AI within character limits. Catches limits broken and invented claims.

stages.title: Copy that worked (or didn't)
stages.summary: Real writing they did and its results. Checks specificity and ownership.

brief.text: You're a copywriter at an agency. The client is **Brewcraft**, launching specialty coffee sold by subscription at ₹2,999. They want a homepage headline and ads.
Research: survey of 189 target customers, "What matters most?"

rows: That the beans are roasted the week they ship

brief.text: "Supermarket coffee tastes flat. I didn't know why until I saw the roast date."
"I want good coffee without thinking about reordering."
Main competitor's headline: "Premium coffee for premium moments."
The company and numbers are fictional, and every candidate gets a slightly different version. A calculator is fine.

prompt.text: Tell us about something you wrote that worked.
Keep it under 45 seconds. This one is not scored; it just gets you talking.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

prompt.text: **Write three different headline directions, then say which one you would put forward and why.** Talk through what you are taking from the research.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

choices.label: Use the client's line as they asked
Ask for proof; if there's none, offer a strong line you can back up
Soften it to "one of India's favourite…"

prompt.text: The client's marketing head loves the work but wants the headline to say **"India's best-tasting coffee"**. There is no data behind it. **What do you do?** Pick one and write what you would say to them.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

variants.label: If they chose "Use the client's line as they asked"

prompt.text: 9 days after launch, a competitor filed a complaint with the advertising standards body about "India's best-tasting coffee". The client asks why the agency didn't warn them.
**What do you do now?**

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

variants.label: If they chose "Ask for proof; if there's none, offer a strong line you can back up"

prompt.text: The client agreed to your line. Ads with it get 2.4% click-through against 1.3% for an old generic line. Now the client wants "15 more versions by tomorrow".
**What do you do now?**

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

variants.label: If they chose "Soften it to "one of India's favourite…""

prompt.text: The client used "one of India's favourite". A customer on social media asks "favourite according to whom?", and the post is getting attention. Click-through is low.
**What do you do now?**

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

variants.label: If they chose "Refuse to write it"

prompt.text: The client went over your head to the agency head, who is annoyed you didn't "find a way". The client's in-house team wrote the No. 1 line themselves.
**What do you do now?**

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

prompt.text: A junior writer drafted this section of the landing page. **Name the biggest problems, worst first.** Then rewrite it (under 60 words).

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

material.text: Leveraging cutting-edge, next-generation technology and a best-in-class, customer-centric approach, Brewcraft brings you a holistic solution designed to empower your lifestyle. Trusted by millions. Oh, and by the way, the beans are roasted the week they ship! So what are you waiting for?? Grab yours today, folks!

prompt.text: Use any AI tool you like for this one. We are assessing how you use it, not whether you do.
Write five search ad headlines (each under 30 characters) and two descriptions (each under 90 characters) for Brewcraft. Count the characters.

items: Paste your full AI conversation, or write "none".
In 2–3 lines, say what you kept, changed or rejected from the AI and why.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

prompt.text: **Tell us about a piece of copy you wrote that worked, or one that didn't, and how you knew.** What did you see, what did you do, and what would you do differently?
Specifics such as numbers and timelines matter more than polish.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.
